about.title: Orange Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Car crashes in Orange follow the shape of the city's traffic. Tustin Street and Chapman Avenue carry much of the local volume, while the SR-55 southbound and SR-22 westbound lanes add freeway-speed collisions to the mix. In 2025, public records show 819 injury collisions inside city limits, with 1,136 people injured and 6 lives lost. Reports cluster on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when the evening commute is heaviest. If one of those collisions was yours, the weeks that follow can feel disorienting: adjusters calling, medical bills arriving, a car you can no longer drive. LawProactive exists for that moment. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Orange County car accident claims and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case recovers money. You keep your focus on healing; the attorney takes on the paperwork, the insurer, and the deadlines.

items.title: Two years sounds long, but it isn't
items.desc: California gives most car crash victims two years to file suit, yet a claim involving a city, county, or Caltrans vehicle can require a government claim in as little as six months. An attorney tracks the right clock from day one.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for the collision; your award is simply reduced by your percentage. Insurers sometimes overstate that percentage, and an attorney pushes back.

items.title: No cap, no upfront fee
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in an ordinary car accident case. Network attorneys work on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hit on the SR-55 near Orange and the other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is usually wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you. Freeway crashes in particular often involve disputed lane changes and speed, so a careful account matters. Let an attorney handle those communications.

items.question: What evidence should I hold onto after a crash on Chapman Avenue or Tustin Street?
items.answer: Keep every photo you took at the scene, the exchange of information, the Orange Police Department or CHP report number, and all medical records and bills. Save the damaged vehicle or at least document it thoroughly before repairs. Nearby businesses on busy corridors may have camera footage that is overwritten within days, so acting quickly can make a real difference.

items.question: The insurer says I was partly at fault. Does that mean I get nothing?
items.answer: No. California follows pure comparative fault, which means your compensation is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated. If you were found 20 percent at fault, for example, you could still recover 80 percent of your damages. An attorney can challenge an unfair fault assignment using the police report, witness accounts, and physical evidence.
